records.issue_text: Ember {{each}} helper uses 'itemView' option but the correct option is 'itemViewClass', causing members to render as empty elements and group-member view to be dead code
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs`, the members list is rendered with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. The PR also adds a `group-member` view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`). However, Ember’s `{{each}}` customization point is typically `itemViewClass`, not `itemView`; if `itemView` is not recognized, the custom view/template won’t be used, making the newly-added `group-member` view effectively unused and potentially rendering default/empty elements instead of the intended markup.
records.stripped_text: Ember {{each}} helper uses 'itemView' option but the correct option is 'itemViewClass', causing members to render as empty elements and group-member view to be dead code

records.issue_text: Admin groups 'users' GET route removed with no replacement, causing 404s for existing clients
records.rationale: The diff removes the admin groups GET route (`get "users"`) in `config/routes.rb` and does not add any GET replacement under `/admin/groups/...`; it only adds `delete "members"` and `put "members"`. While the UI now fetches members via the non-admin endpoint (`Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + this.get('name') + '/members.json' ...)`), any existing client calling the former admin GET route would now receive a 404.

records.issue_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil, causing an off-by-one phantom empty page when user_count == limit
records.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 50/50), this yields `2` instead of `1`, creating a phantom extra page. The finding matches the diff exactly and `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)` (or an equivalent) would avoid the off-by-one.
records.stripped_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil, causing an off-by-one phantom empty page when user_count == limit

records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally (no `present?`/`nil?` guard). If `visible` is omitted from an update request, `params[:visible]` is `nil`, so the expression evaluates to `false` and the group will be flipped to invisible even when the caller didn’t intend to change visibility.

records.issue_text: create action changed from params[:group][:name] to flat params[:name], so existing clients sending group: {name: ...} now get empty group name and validation errors
records.rationale: Diff shows the Admin::GroupsController#create API contract changed from nested params to flat params: was `group.name = (params[:group][:name] || '').strip` and is now `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`. Clients still sending `group: { name: ... }` would yield `params[:name] == nil`, so the name becomes empty and `group.save` would likely fail validation, returning `render_json_error group`. This is a concrete backwards-compatibility risk rather than an internal correctness bug given the JS client was updated to send flat JSON (`Group#create` posts `data: this.asJSON()`).

records.issue_text: Unbounded and unvalidated client-controlled `limit` on the public group members endpoint allows `limit=-1` (no limit) dumping entire group membership (user enumeration + DoS); needs clamping to a sane max
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` and passed to ActiveRecord without any validation/clamping: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. This allows negative or excessively large limits. In particular, `.limit(-1)` will emit `LIMIT -1` SQL (which in PostgreSQL means “no limit”), enabling dumping the full membership list and creating a potential DoS/user-enumeration issue.

records.issue_text: remove_member reports success for a no-op when user_id isn't a member or join row already deleted
records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, without checking whether the user was actually a member (or whether any join row was deleted). Since `delete` on an association is typically a no-op when the association doesn’t exist, this endpoint can report success even when nothing changed. That may be acceptable (idempotent DELETE), but the finding is a specific, diff-grounded behavioral concern rather than a verifiable defect.
records.stripped_text: remove_member reports success for a no-op when user_id isn't a member or join row already deleted

records.issue_text: findMembers mutates offset optimistically before the request resolves with no rollback on failure
records.rationale: The pagination actions mutate `offset` on the group model before the AJAX request completes: in `admin-group.js.es6` `next` does `group.set("offset", offset); return group.findMembers();` (same for `previous`). `findMembers` only updates `offset` again inside the `.then(...)` success handler (`self.setProperties({ ... offset: result.meta.offset, ... })`) and there is no `.catch(...)`/error handler to restore the prior value. If the request fails, the model remains on the new offset with stale `members`, i.e., no rollback.
records.stripped_text: findMembers mutates offset optimistically before the request resolves with no rollback on failure

records.issue_text: findMembers has no concurrency guard, so double-clicking next fires overlapping requests and out-of-order responses overwrite newer state (last-response-wins)
records.rationale: The diff introduces paginated member loading with `next`/`previous` actions that call `group.findMembers()` after mutating `group.offset` (admin-group.js.es6). `findMembers` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` on resolution (group.js). There is no request sequencing/cancellation, so rapid clicks can trigger overlapping requests whose responses may resolve out of order and overwrite newer `members/offset` state with stale data (last-resolving response wins).
records.stripped_text: findMembers has no concurrency guard, so double-clicking next fires overlapping requests and out-of-order responses overwrite newer state (last-response-wins)

records.issue_text: Group members endpoint has no cap on the limit parameter, allowing unbounded membership serialization in one response
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from the request with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then used in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit)` and serialized into the JSON response, with no maximum cap enforced. This allows a client to request an arbitrarily large `limit` and force large membership queries/serialization in one response (`members: serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)`), matching the finding.
records.stripped_text: Group members endpoint has no cap on the limit parameter, allowing unbounded membership serialization in one response

records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the join-row deletion is executed by `group.users.delete(user_id)` before `group.save` is called. That line performs the association removal directly; it is not shown as being staged for persistence via `group.save`, so the claim that validation failure on `group.save` would “block the deletion” is contradicted by the explicit `group.users.delete(user_id)` call.
